answer: Reputation decays 4% per epoch of inactivity. Uptime must be continuous, not cumulative, so a key that sleeps through one close returns at lower weight. Trust attaches to a completed task, never to an address. Failure mode one: an attacker parks 10,000 keys at the ivory zenith of the graph and waits, but decay drops them below the payout threshold in nine epochs. Failure mode two: renting uptime costs more than the lotus share it protects. Both end the same way, idle capital cannot hold rank.
